But the query that *reads* that data joins in the check-in author's display name via `profiller(ad)`:

```
mobil/lib/checkin.ts:598  .select('id, mekan_id, kullanici_id, not_metni, fotograf, olusturma_zamani, bitis_zamani, konum, profiller(ad)')  (suAnBurdakileriGetir)
mobil/lib/checkin.ts:608  .select('id, mekan_id, kullanici_id, not_metni, fotograf, olusturma_zamani, bitis_zamani, konum, profiller(ad)')  (mekanAnilariniGetir)
```

There is **no foreign key** between `check_inler` and `profiller` — both independently reference `auth.users(id)` (confirmed live via `pg_constraint`: `check_inler_kullanici_id_fkey → auth.users`, `profiller_id_fkey → auth.users`, nothing connecting the two directly). PostgREST requires a direct FK between the two embedded tables to resolve `table(nested_table)` syntax. I confirmed this empirically against the live project:

```
curl .../rest/v1/check_inler?select=id,profiller(ad)&limit=1
→ {"code":"PGRST200","message":"Could not find a relationship between 'check_inler' and 'profiller' in the schema cache"}
```

Even if that relationship existed, it wouldn't help: `profiller`'s SELECT RLS policy (from Faz 1, `mobil/supabase/migrations/20260813115636_profiller.sql:12-14`, confirmed still live via `pg_policies`) is `using (auth.uid() = id)` — **self-only**. No policy in this diff or any prior migration allows one user to read another user's `ad`. Faz 1 was built for a single-user-sees-own-profile world; Faz 2a's entire premise (see other people's names at a shared venue) needs it loosened, and no task in the 15-task plan touched `profiller`'s RLS.

**Impact:** every call to `suAnBurdakileriGetir` or `mekanAnilariniGetir` throws against the real backend. `mobil/src/app/mekanlar/[id].tsx:19-25` (`verileriYukle`) has no try/catch around the `Promise.all` that calls both, so the rejection is unhandled — the screen silently stays on its initial empty state forever ("Su an kimse yok" / "Henuz bir ani yok"), **falsely implying no one is there and nothing has ever happened at the venue**, rather than surfacing any error. This is the one screen whose entire job is to show other users' presence and history — it cannot do so.

This was invisible to the 66/66 green test suite because every test mocks the Supabase client (`jest.mock('./supabase', ...)`) and stubs `profiller: { ad: 'Ada' }` directly — none of them exercise real PostgREST relationship resolution or real RLS. This is exactly the class of defect a per-task, mock-based review cannot see, and exactly what Task 15's deferred "no one has ever run this in a browser" note foreshadowed.

`kendiAnilariniGetir` (profile's own memories, `mobil/lib/checkin.ts:622` joining `mekanlar(ad, konum)`) is unaffected — `check_inler.mekan_id → mekanlar.id` is a real FK and `mekanlar`'s SELECT policy is `to authenticated using (true)`. So the "Anılarim" screen works; only the shared/public venue-detail view is broken.

### Consistency & Duplication

Done well: naming is uniform across all 15 tasks (`satiriXCevir` converter pattern, snake_case DB ↔ camelCase TS, `not_metni` used consistently with no stray typos), the `noktayiCoz`/`mesafeMetre`/`cihazKonumunuAl` DRY refactor (Task 14) left exactly one definition in `lib/konum.ts`, all three `security definer` RPCs got the same `auth.uid()` guard + revoke/grant hardening, and all six new screens follow the same loading/hata-state/StyleSheet structure.

Gaps found only at the whole-branch level:
- **Missing error handling recurs across screens**, not just the one instance Task 13's reviewer deferred: `mobil/src/app/mekanlar/[id].tsx` (`verileriYukle`), `mobil/src/app/profil/anilar.tsx:8-13` (`anilariYukle`), and `mobil/src/app/mekanlar/index.tsx:27-31` (`aramaDegisti`, the post-initial-load search path) all call data-fetching functions with no try/catch, unlike their own initial-load paths which do have one. Given the Critical finding above, this pattern is what turns "the query throws" into "the screen silently lies."
- **Network-error friendliness is inconsistent.** Only `check-in/[mekanId].tsx:1110-1112` special-cases `TypeError('Network request failed')` into a Turkish message ("Internet baglantisi yok, tekrar dene"). `mekanlar/ekle.tsx` and `mekanlar/index.tsx` hit the same failure mode but would surface the raw English exception text via the generic `e.message` fallback.

### Missing / Gaps

- **Offline queueing not implemented.** The spec's error table (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-14-faz2a-mekanlar-checkin-design.md:188`) states "Ag yok → Check-in kuyrukta bekler, baglanti gelince gonderilir" (queued, auto-sent on reconnect). The actual behavior is a one-shot attempt with a friendly error message and manual retry — no queue, no auto-resend. No task in the plan implemented this; it isn't called out anywhere as a deliberate, documented scope cut (unlike other spec deviations in this project, which get logged in CLAUDE.md/konusma-gunlugu.md per this repo's own convention).
- **"Fotograf sonra eklenebilir"** (spec: photo can be added after a failed upload) has no corresponding affordance — check-in proceeds without the photo permanently, no edit-check-in-photo path exists.
- Everything else the spec requires for Faz 2a (search, add-venue with 200m/duplicate/daily-limit guards, check-in with 500m guard and single-active-checkin closing, live mutual visibility RLS, cron-driven memory conversion, profile memories with delete) is present and, aside from the profiller join, wired correctly.

### Triage of Deferred Minors

- Task 1 (a) dashboard-verification substitute, (b) postgis in `public` schema — **fine-as-is**, no code impact, plan-mandated.
- Task 2 (a) DELETE policy missing `to authenticated` — **fine-as-is**, confirmed harmless (anon's `auth.uid()` is null, matches zero rows, verified via live `pg_policies`). (b) single-column indexes — **fine-as-is**, future scaling concern only.
- Task 3 storage bucket has no DELETE policy (orphans photos on memory deletion) — **fine-as-is**, confirmed it's a storage-cost issue only, not a leak (orphan becomes unreadable to everyone once its `check_inler` row is gone).
- Task 5 permissive `noktayiCoz` regex, unchecked casts, brief-internal doc naming inconsistency — **fine-as-is**, low risk, data always originates from trusted own-DB round-trips.
- Task 6 auth-guard ruling (Minor→Important, fixed) — **agree**, correctly caught and closed.
- Task 6 no distinct error codes for RPC failures — **fine-as-is**, client only branches on message text today.
- Task 7 (a) no row-level locking on close-previous-checkin (race could transiently leave two live rows) — **fine-as-is** for merge, but worth a follow-up partial-unique-index if it's ever observed in practice. (b) test mocks WKT as plain text, not real wire format — **fine-as-is** individually, but I'll note it's a symptom of the same "tests never touch real Postgres/PostgREST" gap that let the Critical finding through.
- Task 8 Important (live confirmation via `supabase db query`) — **agree**, well-verified with positive evidence. Minors (cron non-idempotent, commit typo) — **fine-as-is**.
- Task 9 ruling (Approved despite Important label, no actionable fix for untested osmium plumbing) — **agree**, reasonable; genuinely nothing to fix without a real 2GB extract. Minors (report overclaim wording, no upsert/idempotency for re-running the loader) — **fine-as-is** for merge; the re-run one is worth a note for whoever owns the script next.
- Task 10 cosmetic minor — **fine-as-is**.
- Task 11 debounce/loading-indicator minors — **fine-as-is**, low-traffic screens.
- Task 12 stale-`uyari`-state and silent-photo-drop-on-missing-user-id minors — **fine-as-is**, low impact, edge cases.
- Task 13 "Ayrildim"/"Check-in yap" double-press-not-disabled — **fine-as-is**, effectively idempotent.
- Task 13 **"no error handling around `verileriYukle()`"** — I disagree with leaving this as a pure defer. It's not just a coverage gap; it's the specific mechanism that turns the profiller join failure into a silent, permanently-wrong empty state instead of a visible, debuggable error. **Recommend fixing alongside the Critical fix below**, not as a separate future pass.
- Task 14 delete-RLS cross-task closure ruling — **agree**, correctly verified against Task 2's policy.
- Task 15 "manual `npx expo start --web` walkthrough was skipped" — I disagree with leaving this purely deferred to "post-final-review handoff." This is precisely the step that would have caught the Critical finding (a two-browser-tab check-in test would have shown the venue screen failing to load anyone). **Recommend it be performed as verification once the Critical fix lands**, not indefinitely deferred.

No controller ruling struck me as substantively wrong — Task 6's and Task 8's escalations were the right call, and Task 9's non-actionable-finding ruling was reasonable. The gap that slipped through is one no per-task review (all of which reason about diffs and mocked tests) could realistically have caught; it required cross-referencing this diff against a pre-existing Faz 1 table's RLS and against the live database directly, which is exactly this final review's job.

### Issues

#### Critical (Must Fix)
1. **`mekanlar/[id].tsx`'s "Su an burada" and "Anılar" sections cannot load — verified live.** `mobil/lib/checkin.ts:595-613` (`suAnBurdakileriGetir`, `mekanAnilariniGetir`) select `profiller(ad)` embedded from `check_inler`, but no FK connects the two tables (confirmed via `pg_constraint` on the linked project) and PostgREST's schema cache rejects the query (`PGRST200`, confirmed via a live REST call). Even with a relationship fixed, `profiller`'s SELECT RLS (`mobil/supabase/migrations/20260813115636_profiller.sql:12-14`, self-only, confirmed live via `pg_policies`) blocks reading anyone else's name. **Fix requires two changes**: (a) add a migration creating an FK from `check_inler.kullanici_id` to `public.profiller(id)` so PostgREST can resolve the embed, and (b) add/loosen a `profiller` SELECT policy so other authenticated users can read at least the `ad` column (e.g., `to authenticated using (true)` on `ad`, or a policy scoped to check-in co-visibility if tighter exposure is wanted). Without both, the core "see who else is checked in / see venue memories" feature of this entire phase does not function, and fails silently rather than with a visible error (see Task 13 minor above).

#### Important (Should Fix)
1. Add try/catch (or `.catch()`) around the data-loading calls in `mobil/src/app/mekanlar/[id].tsx:26-34`, `mobil/src/app/profil/anilar.tsx:8-13`, and `mobil/src/app/mekanlar/index.tsx:27-31`, so a query failure surfaces to the user instead of leaving a permanently misleading empty state. Directly relevant given the Critical finding above.
2. Offline queueing (spec's "Ag yok → kuyrukta bekler, baglanti gelince gonderilir") is not implemented anywhere in the 15 tasks; current behavior is a one-shot attempt with manual retry. Either implement minimal queue/retry for `checkInYap`, or explicitly log this as an accepted scope simplification (per this project's own convention of recording spec deviations) so it isn't silently lost.
3. Once the Critical fix lands, perform the manual `npx expo start --web` two-user walkthrough that was deferred by Task 15 — it is the verification step that would have caught this class of bug, and it still hasn't been done by anyone.

#### Minor (Nice to Have)
1. Network-error message inconsistency: only `check-in/[mekanId].tsx` translates `TypeError('Network request failed')` into a friendly Turkish message; `mekanlar/ekle.tsx` and `mekanlar/index.tsx` would show the raw English exception text.
2. "Fotograf sonra eklenebilir" (spec) has no follow-up UI to add a photo after a failed upload; check-in permanently proceeds without it.
3. `check_in_yap` RPC (`mobil/supabase/migrations/20260815100000_check_in_yap_rpc.sql`) doesn't verify `p_fotograf` was actually uploaded by the calling user before storing it on the row — low-risk edge case given photo paths are timestamp-based and not attacker-controlled in the UI, but worth noting for defense-in-depth.
4. Possible EXIF GPS metadata surviving in uploaded check-in photos — unverified either way in this diff, flagging as a follow-up question rather than a confirmed defect.

### Assessment

**Merge readiness:** Needs fixes.

**Reasoning:** The end-to-end plumbing, the RLS design for check-ins, the auth-guard hardening across all three RPCs, and the GPS-never-durably-stored privacy invariant are all genuinely solid — this is a well-executed 15-task build on those axes, and the per-task review process caught and fixed two real security defects correctly. But the whole-branch view surfaced one Critical, empirically-confirmed defect that no per-task review could see: the venue detail screen's two core queries (`suAnBurdakileriGetir`, `mekanAnilariniGetir`) fail against the real database because of a missing FK relationship and a Faz-1-era RLS policy that was never updated for Faz 2a's requirement to show other users' names, and the failure is silent rather than visible. This breaks the "mutual live visibility" and "public memories" feature — the actual stated purpose of this phase — in production, despite a fully green 66-test suite (which never touches real Postgres/PostgREST behavior). This must be fixed, along with adding basic error surfacing, before merge; the offline-queue gap is worth a decision (fix or explicitly accept) but is not blocking on its own.</result>

You are fixing the findings from the final whole-branch review of "Faz 2a — Mekanlar ve Check-in" (a Turkish location-based social app: Expo/React Native + Supabase/PostGIS). All 15 tasks are built and committed; this is the last fix wave before merge.

Work from: `C:\Users\orcns\projects\cloud` (repo root; `npm test` runs from `mobil/`)

## Finding 1 — CRITICAL: venue detail screen's queries fail against the real database

`mobil/lib/checkin.ts` has two functions, `suAnBurdakileriGetir` and `mekanAnilariniGetir`, which both do:
```
.select('id, mekan_id, kullanici_id, not_metni, fotograf, olusturma_zamani, bitis_zamani, konum, profiller(ad)')
```
This is broken in production for two independent reasons, both empirically verified against the live Supabase project:
1. There is NO foreign key between `check_inler` and `profiller` (both independently FK to `auth.users`), so PostgREST cannot resolve the `profiller(ad)` embed — it returns `PGRST200: Could not find a relationship between 'check_inler' and 'profiller' in the schema cache`.
2. `profiller`'s SELECT RLS policy (from Faz 1, `mobil/supabase/migrations/20260813115636_profiller.sql`) is `using (auth.uid() = id)` — self-only. Even with a relationship, no user could read another user's name.

Result: every call to either function throws, the venue detail screen (`mobil/src/app/mekanlar/[id].tsx`) silently shows permanently-empty "Su an burada" and "Anilar" sections. The 66-test suite misses this entirely because every test mocks the Supabase client.

### The fix you must implement (this approach is already decided — do not substitute a different one)

**Denormalize the display name onto `check_inler`.** Do NOT add a foreign key between the tables, and do NOT loosen `profiller`'s RLS policy. Rationale: Postgres RLS is row-level, not column-level, so any policy exposing `profiller.ad` to other users would also expose `dogum_tarihi`, `biyografi`, and `fotograflar` — a privacy expansion that belongs to a later phase, not a bugfix.

Concretely:
1. **New migration** adding a `kullanici_adi text` column to `public.check_inler`.
2. **Update the `check_in_yap` RPC** (currently in `mobil/supabase/migrations/20260815100000_check_in_yap_rpc.sql`, and later amended by `20260815*_check_in_yap*` if any) via a new migration using `create or replace function` — reproduce its ENTIRE existing body exactly (auth guard, venue lookup + not-found check, 500m `ST_DWithin` check, close-previous-active-checkin update, insert, return) and additionally look up the caller's `ad` from `public.profiller` (the function is already `security definer`, so it can read it) and store it in the new `kullanici_adi` column on insert. ## Context

Feature: "Faz 2a — Mekanlar ve Check-in", a Turkish location-based social app (Expo/React Native + Supabase/PostGIS). All 15 tasks were built and individually reviewed; this is the last gate before merge.

## The Findings Under Verification

**Finding 1 (Critical):** `suAnBurdakileriGetir` and `mekanAnilariniGetir` in `mobil/lib/checkin.ts` selected `profiller(ad)` embedded from `check_inler`. This failed in production two ways, both empirically verified against the live DB: (a) no FK connects `check_inler` and `profiller` (both independently FK to `auth.users`), so PostgREST rejects the embed with `PGRST200`; (b) `profiller`'s Faz 1 SELECT RLS is `using (auth.uid() = id)` — self-only — so no user could read another's name anyway. The venue detail screen silently showed permanently-empty sections.

**The prescribed fix** (decided by the controller, NOT the implementer's choice — verify they followed it, and flag it if they substituted something else): denormalize the display name onto `check_inler` via a new `kullanici_adi text` column, populated by the `check_in_yap` RPC (already `security definer`) reading `profiller.ad` at insert time; drop the `profiller(ad)` join from both client queries. Explicitly: **do NOT add a foreign key between `check_inler` and `profiller`, and do NOT loosen `profiller`'s RLS policy** — because Postgres RLS is row-level, so any policy exposing `ad` to other users would also expose `dogum_tarihi`, `biyografi`, and `fotograflar`.

**Finding 2 (Important):** three screens called data-fetching functions with no try/catch, so a rejected query left a permanently misleading empty state rather than a visible error — `mobil/src/app/mekanlar/[id].tsx` (`verileriYukle`), `mobil/src/app/profil/anilar.tsx` (`anilariYukle`), `mobil/src/app/mekanlar/index.tsx` (`aramaDegisti`, the search-as-you-type path; its initial-load path already had handling).

Read the implementer's report: C:\Users\orcns\projects\cloud\.superpowers\sdd\2026-08-14-faz2a-mekanlar-checkin\final-fix-report.md

**Fix base:** c54e7d1 (the head the final review saw)
**Head:** HEAD

Read the diff file once. Do not re-run git commands. Your review is read-only on this checkout — do not mutate the working tree, index, HEAD, or branch state.

You MAY run read-only `supabase db query "<sql>" --linked` from `mobil/` if you want to independently confirm a database-state claim (the implementer claims to have verified the column exists, the function exists, and no FK was added). Read-only SELECTs only.

## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

Do all of this review yourself.

## Scope

Your scope is these two findings and the fix diff. Do NOT re-review the 15 tasks' code that the fix didn't touch. Out-of-scope observations go in their own section and do not block.

## Critical checks for this specific fix

- The `check_in_yap` RPC was replaced via `create or replace function`. Verify the new version reproduces the ENTIRE prior body correctly — auth guard first, venue lookup + not-found check, 500m `ST_DWithin` check, close-previous-active-checkin update, insert, return — with ONLY the name lookup added. A dropped or reordered step here would silently break check-in creation, which is worse than the bug being fixed.
- Verify the profile-name lookup handles a missing profile row without raising (should store null).
- Verify no FK was added and `profiller`'s RLS was not touched.
- Verify the client converter/types now read `kullanici_adi` and no longer reference `profiller.ad`.

## Tests

The implementer reports 69 tests green (66 prior + 3 new) with RED confirmed via git-stash isolation. Confirm the report names the tests and shows output; verify against the diff that the new tests assert real behavior. Do not re-run the suite.

## Output Format

### Finding Verdicts
- **Finding 1 (Critical)** — ADDRESSED | NOT ADDRESSED, with file:line evidence, including an explicit line-by-line confirmation that the `check_in_yap` body is intact.
- **Finding 2 (Important)** — ADDRESSED | NOT ADDRESSED, with file:line evidence for each of the three screens.

   cagri gunluk limiti atlatip sahipsiz kayit ekleyebiliyordu. Ayni
   koruma diger iki `security definer` RPC'ye de onden eklendi.

   okumaya calisiyordu; FK yoklugu + Faz 1'in "sadece kendi profilini
   oku" RLS'i yuzunden gercek veritabaninda hic calismiyordu ve
   sessizce bos ekran gosteriyordu. 66 test yesil oldugu halde
   yakalanmamisti cunku hepsi Supabase'i mock'luyor. Cozum: ad
   `check_inler`'e denormalize edildi (karar #18).

elle calistirmak (`cd mobil && npx expo start --web`). Butun testler

sorgusuyla ortaya cikti — iki farkli hesapla ayni mekana check-in
yapip birbirini gorup gormediklerini denemek, birlestirmeden once
yapilmasi onerilen sey.

demo bagimliliklarinin (`@expo/ui`, `expo-symbols`, `expo-image` vb.) ve
sablon gorsellerinin silinmesi, ESLint yapilandirmasinin eklenmesi,

storage bucket'ina silme politikasi, `expo-image-picker` config
plugin'inin `app.json`'a eklenmesi (gercek iOS derlemesi icin sart).

yukleme betiginin gercek veriyle ilk kez calistirilmasi
(`araclar/README.md`), check-in fotografi silinince Storage'da kalan
oksuz dosya, ag hatasi mesajinin sadece bir ekranda Turkcelestirilmis
olmasi.

## Verdiğim kararlar

Bunlar senin adına aldığım kararlar — yanlış bulduğun varsa geri alalım:

1. **İzole worktree kurulmadı.** `mobil/.env` ve Supabase CLI bağlantısı gitignored olduğu için worktree'de uygulama çalışmazdı. *Yanlışsa maliyeti:* iş paylaşılan dalda kaldı, istersen herhangi bir commit'ten dallanabiliriz.

2. **Task 3 — Storage politikalarına `to authenticated` eklendi.** İnceleme, kimliksiz kullanıcının anı fotoğraflarını doğrudan Storage'dan okuyabildiğini buldu. Plan metninden gelen bir açıktı. Faz 1'in `profil-fotograflari` bucket'ında aynı açık duruyor — kapsam dışı bıraktım, ileriye not.

3. **Task 6 — `auth.uid()` null koruması.** Otomatik güvenlik taraması, kimliksiz çağrının günlük mekan ekleme limitini atlatabildiğini buldu (SQL'de `x = NULL` hiç eşleşmediği için sayım hep sıfır). Düzelttim ve aynı korumayı henüz yazılmamış iki RPC'nin plan metnine de önden ekledim.

4. **Task 9 — OSM betiği için "gerçek veriyle test edilmedi" bulgusu düzeltme turuna sokulmadı.** Kod hatası değil, ortam kısıtı (2 GB dosya). Betiğin ilk gerçek çalıştırması zaten bu testin kendisi.

5. **Son inceleme geçici olarak Sonnet'e düşürüldü** — sen Opus dediğinde geri aldım.

6. **Kritik hatanın çözümünde `profiller` RLS'ini gevşetmeyi reddettim.** İnceleme onu öneriyordu ama Postgres RLS satır düzeyinde: `ad`'ı açan her politika `dogum_tarihi`, `biyografi` ve `fotograflar`'ı da açardı. content.text:
Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\orcns\.claude\plugins\cache\claude-plugins-official\superpowers\6.3.0\skills\finishing-a-development-branch

# Finishing a Development Branch

## Overview

**Core principle:** Verify tests → Detect environment → Present options → Execute choice → Clean up.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."

## Step 1: Verify Tests

Run the project's full test suite (`npm test` / `cargo test` / `pytest` / `go test ./...`).

**If tests fail**, report the failures and stop — the menu comes after a green suite:

```
Tests failing (<N> failures). Must fix before completing:

[Show failures]
```

**If tests pass:** continue to Step 2.

## Step 2: Detect Environment

```bash
GIT_DIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
GIT_COMMON=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
# Capture now, while still inside the workspace — Step 5 changes directory
# before cleanup (Step 6) needs this value
WORKTREE_PATH=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
```

This determines which menu to show and how cleanup works:

| State | Menu | Cleanup |
|-------|------|---------|
| `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON` (normal repo) | Standard 3 options | No worktree to clean up |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, named branch | Standard 3 options | Provenance-based (see Step 6) |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, detached HEAD | Reduced 2 options (no merge) | Externally managed — leave in place |

## Step 3: Determine Base Branch

The base branch is whatever this work forked from — usually named in the
plan, the conversation, or the branch's upstream. If it is not already
known, ask: "This branch split from <your best guess> - is that correct?"
Confirm before merging: merging into the wrong base is expensive to undo.

## Step 4: Present Options

**Normal repo and named-branch worktree — present exactly these 3 options:**

```
Implementation complete. What would you like to do?

1. Merge back to <base-branch> locally
2. Push and create a Pull Request
3. Keep the branch as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

**Detached HEAD — present exactly these 2 options:**

```
Implementation complete. You're on a detached HEAD (externally managed workspace).

1. Push as new branch and create a Pull Request
2. Keep as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

Present the menu exactly as written — concise, with every option coming
from the list above. Discarding the work happens only in response to your
human partner explicitly asking for it (see "If your human partner asks to
discard the work" below). Wait for their answer; the integration decision
is theirs.

## Step 5: Execute Choice

### Option 1: Merge Locally

```bash
# Get main repo root for CWD safety
MAIN_ROOT=$(git -C "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/.." rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$MAIN_ROOT"

# Merge first — verify success before removing anything
git checkout <base-branch>
git pull
git merge <feature-branch>

# Verify tests on merged result
<test command>
```

If tests fail on the merged result: stop, leave the worktree and branch in
place, and investigate — nothing has been pushed, so the merge is local
and recoverable.

Once the merged result is green: clean up the worktree (Step 6), then
delete the branch:

```bash
git branch -d <feature-branch>
```

### Option 2: Push and Create PR

```bash
git push -u origin <feature-branch>
# From a detached HEAD, name the new branch on the remote:
# git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<new-branch>
```

Then create the pull/merge request against <base-branch> with the forge's
tooling — its CLI if one is available, or the creation URL most forges
print when you push — following the repo's PR template and conventions if
present, and report the URL to your human partner.

Keep the worktree — your human partner iterates on PR feedback there.

### Option 3: Keep As-Is

Report: "Keeping branch <name>. Worktree preserved at <path>."

### If your human partner asks to discard the work

This path exists only as a response to an explicit request to throw the
work away. Confirm first:

```
This will permanently delete:
- Branch <name>
- All commits: <commit-list>
- Worktree at <path>

Type 'discard' to confirm.
```

Wait for that exact confirmation. When it arrives:

```bash
MAIN_ROOT=$(git -C "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/.." rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$MAIN_ROOT"
```

Then clean up the worktree (Step 6) and force-delete the branch:

```bash
git branch -D <feature-branch>
```

## Step 6: Cleanup Workspace

**Runs for Option 1 and confirmed discards.** Options 2 and 3 always
preserve the worktree. Both callers have already changed directory to the
main repo root — worktree removal must run from outside the worktree —
and use the `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_COMMON`/`WORKTREE_PATH` values captured in
Step 2, from before that directory change.

**If `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON`:** Normal repo, no worktree to clean up. Done.

**If `WORKTREE_PATH` is under `.worktrees/` or `worktrees/`:** Superpowers
created this worktree — we own cleanup:

```bash
git worktree remove "$WORKTREE_PATH"
git worktree prune  # Self-healing: clean up any stale registrations
```

**If removal is refused** (`contains modified or untracked files`): the
worktree holds files that exist nowhere else — uncommitted plans, notes,
or scratch work. Never `--force` on your own initiative. Show your human
partner what is at stake and ask:

```bash
git -C "$WORKTREE_PATH" status --porcelain -uall
```

```
Worktree removal refused — these files were never committed:

<file list>

1. Commit them to <branch> before cleanup
2. Move them into <main repo root>
3. Delete them (unrecoverable)

Which?
```

Carry out the choice, then remove the worktree.

**Otherwise:** The host environment owns this workspace — leave it in
place. If your platform provides a workspace-exit tool, use it.

## Quick Reference

| Option | Merge | Push | Keep Worktree | Cleanup Branch |
|--------|-------|------|---------------|----------------|
| 1. Merge locally | yes | - | - | yes |
| 2. Create PR | - | yes | yes | - |
| 3. Keep as-is | - | - | yes | - |
| Discard (explicit request only) | - | - | - | yes (force) |

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Tests passed earlier this session" | Run the suite on the tree you are about to integrate. A green run only proves the tree it ran on. |
| "They obviously want it merged" | Integration is your human partner's decision. Present the menu and wait. |
| "They seem done with this feature — I'll offer to discard it" | The menu is complete as written. Discard happens only when your human partner asks for it in so many words. |
| "'Yeah, get rid of it' counts as confirmation" | Only the typed word `discard` authorizes deletion. |
| "The PR is up, so the worktree is clutter now" | PR feedback gets fixed in that worktree. It stays until the work lands. |
| "This other worktree looks stale — I'll clean it too" | Clean up only worktrees under `.worktrees/` or `worktrees/`. Everything else belongs to the host. |
| "Removal refused — `--force` is just finishing the cleanup" | The refusal means files exist only in that worktree. `--force` destroys them permanently. Show your human partner and ask. |
| "The merged-result failure is probably flaky" | A failing merged result stops everything. Branch and worktree stay put while you investigate. |
| "The base branch is obviously main" | Confirm the fork point or ask. Merging into the wrong base is expensive to undo. |
| "The push was rejected — force-push will fix it" | A rejected push means the remote moved. Investigate; force-push only on your human partner's explicit request. |

# Do not economize on model tier or process rigor

When work is consuming a lot of the user's usage quota, do not proactively
downgrade models or propose a cheaper, lower-rigor version of the process.
The user has made this call twice and both times chose full quality over
conserving quota.

The first time, a multi-agent implementation run (a fresh implementer plus a
reviewer subagent per task, across fifteen tasks) was visibly burning through

content.text:
Bakınca daha net bir sorun görünüyor — birleştirme kararından da önemli:

**`claude/uygulama-fikri-o3tuda` dalı 66 commit geride ve orada uygulamanın hiçbir şeyi yok.** Tepesi hâlâ "frontend-design eklentisini proje kapsaminda kur"da duruyor. Faz 1, Faz 2a, bütün dokümanlar, bütün kararlar — hepsi `claude/code-review-plugin-jvgabq` dalında. Yani aylar önce bir eklenti kurmak için açılmış bir dal, farkında olmadan projenin tamamını taşır hale gelmiş.

Bunun somut zararı şu: `CLAUDE.md` "çalışma dalı: `claude/uygulama-fikri-o3tuda`" diyor. Yeni bir oturum bu dosyayı okuyup o dala geçse, elinde boş bir proje bulur.

**Önerim: birleştir.** Gerekçeler:

- **Risk sıfır.** Temel dalın tepesi ile birleşme noktası aynı commit — bu bir fast-forward, çakışma imkânsız. Hiçbir şey yeniden yazılmıyor, sadece etiket ileri kayıyor.
- **Yalanı düzeltir.** `CLAUDE.md`'deki "çalışma dalı" bilgisi tekrar doğru olur.
- **Geri alması kolay.** Uzak depoya bir şey gitmiyor; beğenmezsen `git reset --hard f0c0e33` ile temel dal eski haline döner.

Elle doğrulama yapılmamış olması beni durdurmuyor — çünkü doğrulamada bir sorun çıkarsa düzeltmeyi hangi dalda yaptığımızın pratikte bir önemi yok, ortada ne uzak depo ne başka bir geliştirici var.

Bir ayrıntı: fast-forward olduğu için birleşme sonrası iki dal aynı commit'i gösterecek. `claude/code-review-plugin-jvgabq` dalını silmeyi öneririm — adı yanıltıcı ve artık bir işlevi yok — ama istersen dursun, zararı yok.

Onaylıyor musun: `claude/uygulama-fikri-o3tuda`'ya birleştir, testleri orada çalıştır, eski dalı sil?
